messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 paging eng-sre: alert: latency_regression on /v1/generate - p50 210ms -> 600ms, p95 420ms -> 1.1s, error rate +0.2%. Affected: hosted-prod (multiple tenants). Triggered at 2026-03-15T09:20:34Z
Sam (on-call): I’m on it. pulling up dashboards. assigning to @Anya for triage.
Anya (eng-sre): taking lead. Sam, can you confirm whether this is global or region-specific? Also any recent deploys?
Sam (on-call): Appears to be mostly us-east-1. No deploys in the last 3 hours per deploy-bot. Initial mitigation: bumped the dedicated pool autoscale to +30% to absorb traffic.
Kevin (eng-runtime): I’m seeing a backend signal: queue depth spiking on inference-workers-*-us-east. p95 token latency rise correlates with host-level syscall wait increases. grabbing perf counters and top.
Maria (eng-platform): Noted customer pager for tenant "stark-analytics" opened at T+4m. Support says they see timeouts after 1s. Prioritized for severity=P2.
Anya (eng-sre): timeline so far:
- 09:20:34Z alert fired (incident-bot)
- 09:21:10Z autoscale bump +30%
- 09:22:05Z on-call acknowledgment
- 09:24:00Z initial p95 >1s observed across 60% hosts us-east
- ongoing
Anya (eng-sre): hypothesis 1: kernel scheduler regression on a subset of hosts after last kernel patch last night. hypothesis 2: noisy co-tenant causing CPU steal. hypothesis 3: runtime memory pressure causing GC stalls (less likely).
Sam (on-call): Kevin, can you share `dmesg` / kernel logs and perf top sample?
Kevin (eng-runtime): pasting snippets:
```
# ssh inference-host-12
$ uname -a
Linux inference-host-12 6.1.0-rc1-custom #45 SMP Tue Mar 14 04:12:10 UTC 2026 x86_64 GNU/Linux
$ sudo journalctl -u nri-inference -n 200 | grep -i warn
2026-03-15T09:18:02Z nri-inference[1234]: KV cache miss spike start
2026-03-15T09:20:20Z nri-inference[1234]: slow-queue: worker-8 latency 1.2s
```
`perf stat` across affected host pool (1m):
```
cycles: 1.2e9
instructions: 6.1e8
context-switches: 42k  <-- baseline ~4k
CPU-migrations: 4k
page-faults: 120
```
Kevin (eng-runtime): context-switches up 10x. That smells like scheduler contention or heavy irq/softirq load. Also seeing higher `softirqs` in /proc/softirqs.
Anya (eng-sre): useful. Any recent host-level kernel updates? Maria?
Maria (eng-platform): We rolled kernel 6.1.0-rc1-custom to a canary subset (10% of hosts) at 02:00Z for testing and then promoted to 50% at 07:30Z due to earlier perf improvements. Rolling back on canary started last hour but not finished.
Sam (on-call): ok that aligns: promoted earlier in the day, and now p95 hit across 60% hosts — could be a bad kernel build. Can we identify which hosts are on the promoted kernel and isolate?
Kevin (eng-runtime): running quick query: `hosts | where kernel=="6.1.0-rc1-custom" and region=="us-east-1"` -> 48 hosts. Marking them as suspect.
Anya (eng-sre): mitigation plan A: drain and reprovision a small subset (5 hosts) back to previous kernel and observe p95 on traffic pinned to those hosts. Plan B (if high customer impact): global rollout pause + route traffic to other regions or serve degraded model.
Maria (eng-platform): can do immediate rollback for 5 hosts. Also we can enable request-routing preference to avoid those kernel hosts (manual host-tag avoid).
Sam (on-call): quick mitigation enacted: routing rule added to prefer us-west pools for new requests, also temporarily extended request timeout to 2s for tenant "stark-analytics" to reduce client errors.
Anya (eng-sre): Kevin, please run a trace sample of a slow request (trace id) and paste spans. Looking for long scheduler_wait or syscall durations.
Kevin (eng-runtime): trace sample:
```
Span: /v1/generate -> runtime.dispatch (50ms) -> runtime.kv_fetch (120ms) -> kernel.syscall (540ms) -> runtime.tokenize (30ms)
```
Kevin (eng-runtime): kernel.syscall is the big chunk. On unaffected hosts kernel.syscall shows ~20ms.
Anya (eng-sre): that’s convincing for kernel-level regression. Hypothesis weight: kernel regression 0.8, noisy tenant 0.15, runtime GC 0.05.
Sam (on-call): customer impact update: support reports errors dropped from 12% -> 3% after routing to us-west. Still seeing p95 degradation for in-flight sessions bound to old hosts.
Maria (eng-platform): performing the 5-host rollback now (in progress). Rolling back images and re-running smoke tests. ETA ~10m.
Ops Pager: acknowledged. If rollback confirms, we should trigger a hold on the kernel rollout and notify infra.
Kevin (eng-runtime): also collected `perf record` on a suspect host; I’ll upload to the shared bucket: s3://redwood-infra/incident-1962501234/perf/inference-host-12.data
Anya (eng-sre): next steps to close incident:
- validate rollback effect on p95 on targeted hosts (monitoring)
- if p95 returns to baseline, pause kernel promotion and open kernel-rca ticket with infra/kernel team
- communicate customer-facing postmortem and mitigation to affected tenants
- create follow-up test to reproduce syscall stall under load (stress and perf)
Sam (on-call): thanks team. I’ll keep paging channel open and will post a final status when rollback completes or if we need escalation to execs.
Maria (eng-platform): rollback completed on 5 hosts at 09:34:50Z. Early metrics: p95 on those hosts dropped from 1.05s -> 230ms over next 90s.
Anya (eng-sre): excellent — that strongly points to kernel regression. Pausing rollout globally and notifying kernel owners. I’ll start an in-incident RCA thread with timeline, commands, and perf artifacts.
Sam (on-call): closing paging alerts. Creating follow-up: ticket INF-3912 (kernel-p95-regression) and assigning to infra-kernel.
Kevin (eng-runtime): uploaded perf artefacts and trace snippets to the ticket. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3912
Anya (eng-sre): final note: customers should be informed about potential transient errors during rollback window. Support will send templated email. :thumbsup:
Sam (on-call): thanks all. good runbook execution. will mark this thread resolved but keep it for RCA notes.
